The amending arrêté n° 2015-4534/GNC-Pr of 20 April 2015 is listed by the NC maritime affairs website (per a search result) but its text could not be downloaded (dam.gouv.nc and juridoc returned errors), so any change it made is unknown.
nt: Use with care. (1) The 2015 amendment by the Government of New Caledonia was not read; it may have changed the notice, the addresses or the format. (2) All contacts printed in the 2006 text (lagoon.nc e-mails, fax 687.29.23.03, Nouméa Radio FJP) are probably out of date; MRCC Nouméa became COSS NC by arrêté of 30 December 2022, and its website says to report to noumea.traffic@mrcc.nc. (3) The notice is counted from entry into INTERNAL waters (inside the reef baselines), not the 12 NM limit. Other rules in the 2006 text: Art. 3, tankers in territorial waters with no intention to go to a pilot boarding point keep more than 7 NM outside the baselines of the Grande Terre and isolated islands or reefs (Loyalty Islands: only between Ouvéa and Lifou, 7 NM off); Art. 4.2, any tanker suffering damage or failure in internal or territorial waters or within 50 NM of their outer limit informs the MRCC at once (Annex 2); Art. 5, tankers are forbidden in internal waters except listed port access (Nouméa, Prony, Népoui, Loyalty Islands) with day-only, tonnage and draught limits and compulsory pilotage 3 NM off the passes. Wallis and Futuna was not researched.

t: SURNAV France: Mediterranean (incl. Corsica)
au: Préfet maritime de la Méditerranée (Toulon); reports go to CROSS MED (MRCC La Garde)
ap: The entry notice (Art. 2.1) is for the master of any ship in Art. 1 §1.1 about to pass through or stay in French territorial or internal waters of the Mediterranean: oil tankers carrying oil listed in MARPOL Annex I Appendix I; ships carrying noxious liquid substances of MARPOL Annex II in categories X or Y of IBC Code chapter 17; ships carrying an INF cargo (as defined in Art. 221-VII/14 of the French ship safety rules) or the dangerous substances of Annex I (plutonium 239, uranium 233, 235, 238, thorium and material containing them except ores; in bulk: acetaldehyde, ethyl ether, ethyl vinyl ether, monoethylamine, ammonium nitrate, propylene oxide); incinerator ships carrying organochlorine compounds; ships carrying liquefied gases in bulk; tankers that are not inerted. No tonnage limit is given for the notice. The Art. 3 message (Annex IV) is for every ship in Art. 1, including §1.2 (other MARPOL Annex II and III substances, IMDG, IBC ch. 17, IGC ch. 19 goods), coming from a port or anchorage outside the EU and planning to anchor in French territorial or internal waters.
apq: 1.1. Aux navires suivants : - navires-citernes transportant des hydrocarbures, dont la liste est fixée par l'appendice I de l'annexe I de la convention [...] (MARPOL 73/78) ; - navires transportant des substances liquides nocives définies par l'appendice II de l'annexe II de la convention MARPOL 73/78 et classées dans les catégories X ou Y au chapitre 17 du recueil [...] IBC ; - navires transportant, une cargaison « INF », telle que définie à l'article 221-VII/14 de la division 221 du règlement annexé à l'arrêté du 23 novembre 1987, ou des substances dangereuses dont la liste figure en annexe I du présent arrêté ; - navires incinérateurs transportant des composés organochlorés ; - navires transportant en vrac des gaz liquéfiés ; - navires-citernes non inertés. [...] 2.1. Le capitaine de tout navire visé au paragraphe 1.1 de l'article 1 du présent arrêté s'apprêtant à passer ou à séjourner dans les eaux territoriales ou intérieures françaises de la Méditerranée est tenu d'adresser au CROSS MED (Centre Régional Opérationnel de Surveillance et de Sauvetage Méditerranée - MRCC LA GARDE) (coordonnées figurant en annexe II du présent arrêté) un message du modèle figurant en annexe III

t: SURNAV France: North Sea, Channel and Atlantic coasts
au: Préfet maritime de l'Atlantique (Brest) and Préfet maritime de la Manche et de la mer du Nord (Cherbourg); reports go to CROSS Gris-Nez, Jobourg, Corsen or Etel
ap: The entry notice (Art. 2) is for the master of any ship in Art. 1 §1 and §2 that is about to pass through or stay in French territorial waters: (1) ships carrying oil or oil gas residues listed in MARPOL Annex I; (2A) ships carrying noxious liquid substances of MARPOL Annex II that are in categories A and B in chapter 17 of the IBC Code; (2B) ships carrying the dangerous substances of decree 79-703 listed in Annex A (plutonium 239, uranium 233, 235, 238, thorium and any material containing them except ores; in bulk: acetaldehyde, ethyl ether, ethyl vinyl ether, monoethylamine, ammonium nitrate, propylene oxide; organochlorine compounds; liquefied gases in bulk); (2C) tankers that are not inerted. No tonnage limit is given for the notice. A second message (Art. 3, Annex E) is for every ship in Art. 1, including §3 (other MARPOL Annex II and III substances, IMDG, IBC ch. 17 and IGC ch. 19 dangerous goods), coming from a port or anchorage outside the EU and planning to anchor in French territorial waters.
apq: Article 1er : Le présent arrêté s'applique : 1) aux navires transportant des hydrocarbures ou des résidus gazeux d'hydrocarbures dont la liste est fixée par l'annexe 1 de la convention internationale pour la prévention de la pollution par les navires [...] (MARPOL 73) ; 2) A - aux navires transportant des substances liquides nocives définies par l'annexe 2 de la convention MARPOL et classées dans la catégorie A et B au chapitre 17 du recueil [...] IBC ; B - aux navires transportant des substances dangereuses telles que définies aux 2°, 3°, 4° et 5° de l'article premier du décret n° 79-703 du 7 août 1979, dont la liste figure en annexe A du présent arrêté ; C - aux navires citernes non inertés. [...] Article 2 : Le capitaine de tout navire visé aux § 1) et 2) de l'article 1er du présent arrêté s'apprêtant à passer ou à séjourner dans les eaux territoriales françaises est tenu d'adresser au centre régional opérationnel de surveillance et de sauvetage (CROSS) géographiquement compétent, tel que défini à l'annexe F, un message du modèle figurant en annexe B et précisant entre autres [...] : - ses intentions de mouvement dans les eaux territoriales ; - l'état de ses capacités de manœuvre et de navigation.

when.x: Six hours before entering French territorial waters if the ship comes from outside.
Six hours before sailing, if the ship is about to sail from a port or from an anchorage, waiting or lightening area on the French coast.

If the movement intentions or the manoeuvring and navigation capabilities change after the message was sent, the master must send a new message at once, in the same way, correcting the first.

Any ship in Art. 1 coming from a port or anchorage outside the EU and planning to anchor in French territorial waters: when it leaves the loading port (or as soon as possible if the destination changes), send the CROSS a message with all the Annex E information, or say which EU authority holds it.

ver: Both prefecture PDFs of the 2002 arrêté downloaded and read in full (text layer); Annex B and Annex F identical in both. Status checked on both prefecture arrêté lists with the 'in force' filter (58/2002 and 2002-099 listed, not marked repealed; only later change found is the 2004 amendment, which removes Art. 9 only). Email, phone and fax of the four CROSS taken from IMO MSC.5/Circ.13 (2014) because the arrêté's 2002 addresses are dead domains; faxes and three of four phone numbers agree with the arrêté. VHF channels are as printed in the 2002 Annex F only.
nt: Rules (who, when, lines) are high confidence: an official text listed as in force. Contacts are medium: the arrêté's own e-mail addresses (equipement.gouv.fr, wanadoo.fr) and telex are obsolete, and the current @mrccfr.eu addresses come from an IMO circular of 2014, not from the arrêté; check with the CROSS if a message bounces. The CROSS is chosen by where the ship comes from or goes to (Annex F), not by position. Categories 'A and B' of MARPOL Annex II are the pre-2007 categories (now X and Y); the arrêté has not been updated. Other rules in the same arrêté: Art. 6, while in French territorial or internal waters (except alongside), keep watch on VHF DSC CH 70, MF DSC 2187.5 kHz and VHF CH 16 and answer French State ships and coast stations; Art. 7, ships of §1 and §2 over 3000 UMS or 1600 TJB keep at least 7 NM from the French coast in territorial waters, except in the north-east lane of the Pas-de-Calais TSS and in passages and channels set by special arrêtés (e.g. arrêté 18/2008 for Le Havre-Antifer, Le Havre, Rouen and Caen); Art. 10, a ship assisting or towing an Art. 1 ship within 50 NM of the French coast informs the CROSS at once (Annex D). This national notice is in addition to the IMO systems in the same waters (WETREP, CALDOVREP, OUESSREP/MANCHEREP) and to EU/port pre-arrival notifications. Penalty: Code des transports Art. L5242-7 (master of a ship carrying hydrocarbons or other dangerous substances entering territorial waters without reporting); wording seen only in a 2015 Légifrance snapshot, Légifrance was not reachable to re-check. The Annex B line B wording 'six chiffes' is a typo in the original for 'six chiffres'.

au: Préfet de la Martinique, délégué du Gouvernement pour l'action de l'État en mer aux Antilles; reports go to CROSS Antilles-Guyane (MRCC Fort-de-France)
ap: The SURNAV notice (Art. 4, Annex II) is for the master of any ship in Art. 1 §2 about to pass through or stay in French territorial waters of the Antilles maritime zone: ships carrying dangerous or polluting goods, oil, or dangerous or polluting oil gas residues as defined by the conventions, codes and protocols in force, however stowed, and empty tankers and empty towed craft carrying or having carried dangerous or polluting goods. Art. 1 as a whole covers commercial ships (and towed craft) of 300 GT or more, passenger ships of 80 m or more and yachts of 80 m or more; §2 begins with 'notamment' (in particular), so read it as the dangerous-goods ships among them. Passenger ships and yachts of 80 m or more send a different message, 'SURNAV CROISIERE' (Art. 8, Annex III). Warships and French State ships on non-commercial public service are exempt (Art. 2).
apq: Article 1 : Le présent arrêté s'applique, dans les limites de la zone économique exclusive (ZEE) française des Antilles et dans la zone de recherche et de sauvetage relevant du Centre régional opérationnel de surveillance et de sauvetage Antilles-Guyane (CROSS AG) : 1. à tous les navires, y compris engins remorqués, d'une jauge brute supérieure ou égale à 300, effectuant une navigation commerciale ; 2. notamment aux navires transportant des marchandises dangereuses ou polluantes, des hydrocarbures ou résidus gazeux d'hydrocarbures dangereux ou polluants au sens des conventions, codes et protocoles en vigueur quel que soit leur mode de stockage, ainsi qu'aux navires citernes lèges et engins remorqués lèges transportant ou ayant transporté des matières dangereuses ou polluantes ; 3. à tous les navires à passagers d'une longueur supérieure ou égale à 80 mètres ; 4. à tous les navires de plaisance d'une longueur supérieure ou égale à 80 mètres. [...] Article 4 : Le capitaine de tout navire visé au paragraphe 2. de l'article 1 s'apprêtant à passer ou à séjourner dans les eaux territoriales françaises de la zone maritime Antilles est tenu de signaler au CROSS AG, par un message conforme au modèle figurant en annexe II et acheminé selon les dispositions de l'annexe I : 1. ses intentions de mouvement dans les eaux territoriales ; 2. sa cargaison ; 3. l'état de ses capacités de manœuvre et de navigation.

when.x: The message must reach CROSS AG at least six hours before entering French territorial waters if the ship comes from outside.
At least six hours before sailing if the ship is about to leave these territorial waters from a port or from an anchorage, waiting or lightening area.
Any change to the programme given in the message must be reported to CROSS AG at once by a correcting message, same model and same way as the first.
Passenger ships and yachts of 80 m or more (Art. 8, 'SURNAV CROISIERE', Annex III): at least six hours before entering the territorial waters of the Antilles maritime zone if coming from outside.
Passenger ships and yachts of 80 m or more (Art. 8): at least one hour before sailing from a port or from an anchorage, waiting or lightening area.

nt: Other rules in the same arrêté: Art. 3, all Art. 1 ships keep a permanent watch on VHF 16 in the territorial and internal waters (also at anchor, not alongside); Art. 5, §2 ships of 3000 GT or more keep more than 7 NM off the coast in territorial waters and cross the 7 NM band by the most direct route when approaching or leaving a French port; Art. 6, between two ports of the same island with a pilot on board they may go inside 7 NM if the Art. 4 information was sent; Art. 7, bunkering or crew change allowed between 5 and 7 NM if stated in the Art. 4 message; Art. 9, passenger ships of 80 m or more keep more than 2 NM off; Art. 10, anchoring outside a port regulation zone is requested from CROSS AG with the message; Art. 11, incidents reported at once (Annex IV). This arrêté repealed arrêté 2014-197-005 of 15 March 2014. Penalties: 'peines prévues par les lois et règlements en vigueur' (Art. 15). t: SURNAV French Polynesia and Clipperton
au: Haut-commissaire de la République en Polynésie française, délégué du Gouvernement pour l'action de l'État en mer; reports go to JRCC Tahiti
ap: The SURNAV notice (Art. 5, Annex 3) is for the master of every ship of Art. 2.2 preparing to transit French territorial waters of French Polynesia and La Passion-Clipperton: ships over 15 m length overall engaged in commercial navigation of 3000 UMS (GT) or more, whatever the cargo; the list of dangerous goods is added where applicable. Not for State ships or ships on public service missions, and (except the incident reporting of Art. 4) not for ships on coastal trade and island service within the territorial waters of French Polynesia (Art. 2).
apq: 2.1 tous les navires d'une longueur hors tout supérieure à 15 mètres naviguant dans les eaux sous souveraineté ou juridiction française, situées au large de la Polynésie française et de l'île de La Passion-Clipperton ; 2.2 parmi les navires visés en 2.1, aux navires effectuant une navigation commerciale, d'une jauge brute égale ou supérieure à 3000 UMS ; [...] Il ne s'applique pas, hormis les dispositions de l'article 4, aux navires effectuant des navigations de cabotage et de desserte maritime dans les eaux territoriales de Polynésie française. [...] Article 5 : Le capitaine de tout navire visé à l'article 2.2 s'apprêtant à transiter dans les eaux territoriales françaises de la Polynésie française et de l'île de La Passion-Clipperton est tenu de signaler à l'autorité maritime, par un message conforme au modèle figurant en annexe 3 et acheminé selon les dispositions de l'annexe 1 : 1. ses intentions de mouvement dans les eaux territoriales ; 2. l'état de ses capacités de manœuvre et de navigation ; 3. le cas échéant, la liste des marchandises dangereuses transportées à bord.

when.x: The message must reach JRCC Tahiti at least 48 hours before entering the territorial waters if the ship comes from outside.
At least 2 hours before sailing if the ship is about to leave these territorial waters from a port or from an anchorage, waiting or lightening area off the French coast.
Any change to the programme given in the message must be reported to JRCC Tahiti at once by a correcting message, same model and same way as the first.

Passenger ships and large yachts of 45 m or more or 300 UMS or more (Art. 2.4) that want to anchor or stop in the territorial waters of French Polynesia: foreign flag ask for authorisation, French flag declare, using the Annex 4 model ('SURNAV – MOUILLAGE / STATIONNEMENT'), between 12 and 24 hours ahead. Maximum stay 24 hours unless stated otherwise (foreign flag). Report arrival at and departure from the anchorage to JRCC Tahiti.

t: SURNAV La Réunion (South Indian Ocean maritime zone)
au: Préfet de La Réunion, délégué du Gouvernement pour l'action de l'État en mer dans la zone maritime sud de l'océan Indien; reports go to CROSS SOI (MRCC La Réunion)
ap: Ships carrying dangerous goods, defined as ships over 300 UMS (gross tonnage) carrying dangerous goods, dangerous substances in bulk or in packages, oil or oil gas residues within the meaning of MARPOL, IMDG, IBC, BC, IGC and INF, that intend to enter the territorial and internal waters adjacent to La Réunion (Art. 2.2, Art. 5.2). The arrêté as a whole applies to ships of 300 UMS or more, or over 24 m, French or foreign, in the French EEZs of the South Indian Ocean and in the territorial and internal waters adjacent to La Réunion (Art. 3.1). State and war ships, ships under 24 m, yachts, and ships in a place of refuge procedure or giving assistance are excluded (Art. 3.3).
apq: 2.2. Navire transportant des matières dangereuses : les navires de jauge supérieure à 300 UMS transportant des matières dangereuses, substances dangereuses en vrac ou en colis, des hydrocarbures ou des résidus gazeux d'hydrocarbures au sens des conventions, codes et protocoles MARPOL, IMDG, IBC, BC, IGC, INF en vigueur. [...] 5.2. Les navires transportant des matières dangereuses ayant l'intention de pénétrer dans les eaux territoriales et intérieures adjacentes à La Réunion doivent le signaler avec un préavis (article 15) au titre de la prévention des sinistres maritimes au moyen du formulaire en annexe VI. Ces comptes-rendus sont adressés au CROSS SOI dont les coordonnées figurent en annexe VII.

when.x: Before entering the territorial and internal waters adjacent to La Réunion, with advance notice, using the Annex VI form. Art. 5.2 refers to Art. 15 for the notice; Art. 15 sets three working days, but only for the request to approach within 7 NM or anchor within 3 NM. The text gives no number of hours for the Annex VI notice itself (see notes).

Dangerous-goods ships wanting to approach within 7 NM of the coast, or to stop or anchor within 3 NM: send the derogation request (Annex IX form) at least three working days before the planned entry into the 7 NM band, with the movement intentions in territorial waters and the state of manoeuvring and navigation capabilities. If the intentions or capabilities change afterwards, send a new corrected form at once.

Any ship wanting to anchor or stop in the territorial sea (prior authorisation, Art. 10): request at least six hours before entering the French territorial waters adjacent to La Réunion. For a ship that also sends the Annex VI notice, the anchoring request may be attached to it (Art. 14.4).
Anchoring or stopping request when coming from a port or anchorage inside these territorial waters: at least one hour before sailing (Art. 14.1). Late requests may be refused.

ver: Arrêté 2080/2022 downloaded from the prefecture site and read in full (text layer, 25 pages). Heading, letters and contacts copied from Annexes VI, VII and IX. It is the only text listed on the prefecture's page for transit and reporting, and its Art. 20 repeals arrêté 0828 of 16 April 2004 and 2098 of 2 July 2020. The old 6 hour rule was read in the CROSS Réunion 2015 report (secondary), not in the 2004 text itself.
nt: Notice period is unclear in the current text: Art. 5.2 says the notice is given 'avec un préavis (article 15)', but Art. 15 is the three working days rule for approaching within 7 NM or anchoring within 3 NM; no number of hours is printed for the Annex VI notice itself (the Annex VI and VII headings also refer to 'article 13', another cross-reference that does not fit). The repealed 2004 arrêté (828) required 6 hours before entering the 12 NM territorial waters, and the current text keeps 6 hours for anchoring requests. Sending the Annex VI notice at least 6 hours before entry, and three working days ahead whenever you need to come within 7 NM, is a safe reading but is NOT confirmed by the text; ask CROSS SOI. The old addressee 'CROSS RU' / 'CROSSRU' is no longer used: the centre is now CROSS SOI (MRCC La Réunion), though reunion@mrccfr.eu is unchanged. Mayotte: the arrêté applies in all French EEZs of the South Indian Ocean zone (incident reporting Art. 6, general duties Art. 4: VHF 16 and MF 2182 watch, AIS on, report damage to CROSS SOI), but the Annex VI entry notice and the 7 NM rule are written for the territorial waters adjacent to La Réunion; anchoring in the territorial waters of Mayotte and the TAAF is set by separate arrêtés of the préfet de Mayotte and the TAAF administrator (Art. 1.2), which were not found or read. Other rules: Art. 5.1, dangerous-goods ships keep at least 7 NM from the French coast in territorial waters; Art. 11.1, oil and liquefied gas carriers may not anchor or stop in the territorial waters of La Réunion (derogation possible, Art. 11.2); Art. 9.4, no bunkering in these waters except by specific arrêté; Art. 13.1, approach and anchoring forbidden to all ships during a cyclone alert. Penalties: Code des transports L. 5242-1 and following.

ap: Oil tankers of 150 GT and above; all ships of 10,000 GT and above; all other ships of any size carrying hazardous cargo, in bulk or in package.
apq: 1.1 Ships of the following categories are required to participate in the system: .1 all oil tanker ships of 150 gross tonnage and above; .2 all ships of 10,000 gross tonnage and above; and .3 all other ships, irrespective of their size, carrying on board hazardous cargo, in bulk or in package. 1.2 For the purpose of this system, the term "hazardous cargo", as defined in resolution MSC.433(98), means: .1 goods classified in the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code; .2 substances classified in chapter 17 of the International Code for the Construction and Equipment of Ships Carrying Dangerous Chemicals in Bulk (IBC Code) and chapter 19 of the International Code for the Construction and Equipment of Ships Carrying Liquefied Gases in Bulk (IGC Code); .3 oils as defined in MARPOL Annex I; .4 noxious liquid substances as defined in MARPOL Annex II; .5 harmful substances as defined in MARPOL Annex III; and .6 radioactive materials specified in the International Code for the Safe Carriage of Packaged Irradiated Nuclear Fuel, Plutonium and High-Level Radioactive Wastes on Board Ships (INF Code).

when.x: 3.1.3 When entering the Adriatic Sea by crossing northwards the parallel 40° 25'.00 N, the ship shall submit the SP to VTS Brindisi, which shall confirm its reception and make this information available to all other competent shore-based authorities.

3.1.4 When leaving a port inside the area covered by the ADRIREP system the ship shall submit the SP to the nearest competent shore-based authority of the country of the port of departure. The authority receiving this report shall confirm its reception and shall make this information available to other competent shore-based authorities.

3.2.1 The position report (PR) is considered as on demand report. This report is provided upon request from the competent shore-based authorities, and it is used to confirm the correctness of data provided in the sailing plan. Any competent shore-based authority of the ADRIREP interacting with the ships may request a PR.
3.2.1 In addition, the PR shall be provided by the ship to the nearest competent shore-based authority whenever there are changes to the SP during the ship's voyage in the ADRIREP area.

3.3.1.1 when entering a port area or an anchorage area under the responsibility of the port within the ADRIREP area. 3.3.2 The ship shall submit the FR to the nearest competent shore-based authority of the port of arrival when entering a port inside the area covered by the ADRIREP system.
3.3.3 The ship shall submit the FR to VTS Brindisi when leaving the area of the ADRIREP system (south from the latitude 40° 25'.00 N).

ln.x: Ship - Ship's name, call sign, IMO identification number and flag
Date/time (UTC) of the report - A 6-digit group giving date of month (first 2 digits), hours and minutes (last 4 digits) for example - DDHHMM
Present position - A 4-digit group giving latitude in degrees and minutes suffixed with "N" or "S" and a 5-digit group giving longitude in degrees and minutes suffixed with "E" or "W"
Course - A 3-digit group giving the course in degrees
Speed - A 3-digit group giving a speed in knots (Speed in knots and tenths of knots)
Port of departure - LoCode or name of port of departure
Destination and estimated time of arrival - ETA in UTC expressed as in B above, followed by LoCode or Name of port of destination
Route information - To be reported on a voluntary basis by ships sharing their voyage plan in electronic format
Draught of the vessel - draught expressed by a 4-digit group indicating centimetres
Cargo information - The general category of hazardous cargo as described in resolution MSC.433(98) and shown in paragraph 1.2 of this document
Agent - Ship agent or Cargo agent

Size and type - Ship's type, expressed by 2 digits AIS code; Deadweight, expressed by 6 digits group indicating tonnes; Gross tonnage, expressed by 6 digits group indicating tonnes; Length overall, expressed by 3 digits group indicating meters; Breadth, expressed by 3 digits group indicating meters. Example: U/31/020000T/030000T/150M/045M
Total number of persons on board - The total number of crew and other persons on board

Miscellaneous - Any other relevant information, including: Bunker fuel details (characteristics and estimated quantity); Navigational Status; SATCOM (ship's satellite communications available); Brief details of incidents (if any)

fn: Message identifier ADRIREP; report types SP (Sailing plan), PR (Position report), FR (Final report) (Appendix 3). Here FR means Final report (in the 2002 system FR meant First report). The SP uses all lines above. The PR updates designators G, I, L, O, P, T, W and X (para 3.2.3). The FR "shall only include information that the vessel is leaving ADRIREP area and any relevant deviations from the SP" (para 3.3.5). In the last section of the SP ships shall also report any defect, damage, deficiency or limitations and, if necessary, a pollution incident or loss of cargo (para 3.1.7). Primary means: SafeSeaNet web interface; VHF and other means are backup. Voice: English with IMO SMCP (para 5.4).

ver: All text from the IMO PDF of MSC.598(111) (pdftotext). The contact table (Appendix 2) was checked entry by entry, every digit and every e-mail letter, against the rendered PDF page 11 at 150 dpi; the operational area chart (Appendix 1, page 10) was looked at: it shows the boundary as a line across the Strait of Otranto from the Italian to the Albanian coast. The IMO index page MSC 2026-27 lists MSC.598(111) (read 2026-10-26). adrirep.emsa.europa.eu answered on 2026-10-26. Only Bar MRCC (phone and e-mail) and the VTS Croatia phone could be matched with a national publication (Croatian Radio Services 2024); the other contacts are as printed by IMO and were not confirmed on national web sites.
nt: Starts at 0000 UTC on 1 December 2026; until then the 2002 rules apply (record imo-adrirep). MSC.598(111) revises annex 2 of MSC.139(76) in its entirety and revokes it from that date. Main changes: new category of all ships of 10,000 GT and above, and ships of any size with hazardous cargo (was 300 GT and above); no sectors and no sector-crossing reports; reports made electronically through SafeSeaNet (https://adrirep.emsa.europa.eu), VHF as backup; Albania (VTS Durres) and more Italian centres join; reports for ships to or from ports in Bosnia and Herzegovina are made available to Bosnia and Herzegovina, and reports of ships leaving south across 40 25N to Greece (para 3.4.4). Contacts are copied exactly as printed, including spellings (for example "kapiteneria.durres@dpdetare.gov.al" and the phone groupings); they were not confirmed on national web sites except as said in verification. The Croatian Radio Services 2024 give vts-rijeka@pomorstvo.hr and VHF Ch 10, 60 for VTS Croatia (Rijeka), while MSC.598(111) gives vts3@pomorstvo.hr and CH 10. One record covers the whole area because the revised system has one area and no sectors; reports go to VTS Brindisi on entry/exit at 40 25N, or to the nearest authority of the port country. The only printed limit is the parallel 40° 25'.00 N; the rest of the boundary is the coast of the Adriatic Sea. The two end points of that parallel (S-IT, S-AL) are where it meets the coast in Natural Earth 10m land data (computed, inferred), only so the map can close the area; the Albanian end is the west coast of the Karaburun peninsula, so Vlore Bay north of 40 25N is inside. Reference charts: Italian Chart No.435 INT 306 (1993, ED-50) and Croatian Chart No.101 (First Edition 1998, New Edition 2005, New print 2017, Bessel).

t: ADRIREP Adriatic Sea (rules until 30 Nov 2026)
au: ADRIATIC TRAFFIC shore-based authorities: Brindisi Coast Guard, Bar MRCC, Rijeka MRCC, Ancona MRSC, Venezia MRSC, Trieste MRSC, Koper MRCC
ap: Oil tankers of 150 GT and above; ships of 300 GT and above carrying dangerous or polluting goods as cargo, in bulk or in packages.
apq: 1.1 Ships of the following categories are required to participate in the system: - all oil tanker ships of 150 gross tonnage and above; - all ships of 300 gross tonnage and above, carrying on board, as cargo, dangerous or polluting goods, in bulk or in packages. 1.2 For the purpose of this system: - "dangerous goods" means goods classified in the IMDG Code, in Chapter 17 of the IBC Code and in Chapter 19 of the IGC Code; - "polluting goods" means oils as defined in MARPOL Annex I, noxious liquid substances as defined in MARPOL Annex II, harmful substances as defined in MARPOL Annex III.

when.x: Sailing northwards (3.3.1.1): The ship shall transmit the first report to the competent shore-based authority of the interested sector when: - entering the Adriatic Sea by crossing northwards the parallel 40° 25'.00 N; - entering the Adriatic Sea by leaving a port inside the area covered by the system.

Sailing northwards (3.3.1.2): The ship shall transmit the position report to the competent shore-based authorities when: - entering a new sector by crossing northwards its southern borderline, as per annex 2; - entering the port of destination in the area covered by the system.

Sailing southwards (3.3.2.1 and .2): The ship shall transmit the first report to the competent shore-based authority of the interested sector when leaving a port inside the area covered by the system. The shore-based authority to whom the first report shall be transmitted is that of the Country of the port the ship is leaving.

Sailing southwards (3.3.2.4): The ship shall transmit the position reports to the competent shore-based authorities when: - entering a new sector by crossing southwards its northern borderline, as per annex 2; - entering the port of destination in the area covered by the system.
(3.3.1.2 and 3.3.2.4) The ship shall transmit the position report to the competent shore-based authorities when: ... entering the port of destination in the area covered by the system.

Crossing the Adriatic Sea (3.3.3.1): The ship shall send the position report to the closest shore based authority of the country the ship is leaving, which shall inform the maritime authority of the port of destination.

Special cases (3.3.4.1): The ship which, sailing northwards or southwards, enters Sector 5 shall transmit the report to, alternatively, one of the competent authorities as per annex 2, according to where the ship is going to or coming from.

Special cases (3.3.4.2): The ship crossing southwards the latitude 40° 25'.00 N and going out either of Sector 1 or of the area covered by the system shall transmit an additional final position report to Brindisi Coast Guard.

ver: Rules, report formats and the sector table from the IMO PDF of MSC.139(76) Annex 2 (pdftotext), with the sector table checked digit by digit against the rendered PDF page 21 (annex page 20) and the chartlet on page 20 looked at. The IMO index pages of MSC resolutions (read 2026-10-26) show no amendment of ADRIREP before MSC.598(111). Phone numbers and e-mails are not in MSC.139(76); they are copied from MSC.598(111) Appendix 2 (checked against the rendered page 11) and only Bar MRCC and the VTS Croatia phone could be matched with a national publication (Croatian Hydrographic Institute Radio Services 2024). The end points of the 40 25N line on the coast are computed from Natural Earth 10m land (inferred). No Italian official web page on ADRIREP was found.
nt: These are the rules of MSC.139(76) annex 2, in force since 1 July 2003. They are REPLACED at 0000 UTC on 1 December 2026 by MSC.598(111) (see record imo-adrirep-2026): new categories (all ships of 10,000 GT and above, any ship with hazardous cargo), no sectors, electronic reporting through SafeSeaNet. One record with a sector table is used instead of one record per sector because all sectors share one outer boundary (the 40 25N parallel and the coast), the sector limits are only parallels of latitude, and the reports depend on the voyage (northbound, southbound, crossing) rather than on a separate address per area; the sector table is in area.sectors and in "how". The authority names are those of 2002: Bar MRCC was printed as "Yugoslavia" (now Montenegro); Rijeka MRCC is now run as VTS Croatia; Italian MRSCs are now Coast Guard operations rooms and VTS centres; channels in use today may differ from the 2002 table (MSC.598(111) gives VTS Venezia CH 9 and VTS Trieste CH 11). Phone and e-mail entries come from the May 2026 resolution and are given for contact only. The only printed limit is the parallel 40° 25'.00 N; the rest of the boundary is the coast of the Adriatic Sea. The two end points of that parallel (S-IT, S-AL) are where it meets the coast in Natural Earth 10m land data (computed, inferred), only so the map can close the area; the Albanian end is the west coast of the Karaburun peninsula, so Vlore Bay north of 40 25N is inside. Reference charts: Italian Chart No.435 INT 306 (1993, ED-50) and Croatian Chart No. 101 (1998, Bessel).

t: Barents SRS (Barents Area)
au: Vardø VTS centre (NOR VTS, Norwegian Coastal Administration) for the Norwegian monitoring area; Murmansk VTS centre (Federal Agency of Maritime and River Transport) for the Russian Federation monitoring area
ap: Ships of 5,000 GT and above; all tankers; all ships carrying hazardous cargoes; a vessel towing with a tow longer than 200 m; any ship not under command, restricted in ability to manoeuvre or with defective navigational aids. Applies to ships passing through or going to and from ports and anchorages in the area.
apq: 1.1 The following categories of ships passing through or proceeding to and from ports and anchorages in the Barents SRS area are required to participate in the ship reporting system: .1 all ships with a gross tonnage of 5,000 and above; .2 all tankers; .3 all ships carrying hazardous cargoes (paragraph 1.2 refers); .4 a vessel towing when the length of the tow exceeds 200 metres; and .5 any ship not under command, restricted in their ability to manoeuvre or having defective navigational aids. 1.3 Ships not listed above may participate in the ship reporting system (SRS) on a voluntary basis.

when.x: 3.4.2 Reports forwarded prior to entering the area can be submitted at any time after entering the Norwegian Economic Zone or the Russian Federation Exclusive Economic Zone and until one hour before entering the Barents SRS operational area. As the Vessel Traffic Services must be able to handle incoming prior reporting, it will not be possible to undertake pre-entry reports any later than one hour prior to entering the area.
3.4.1 Ships entering the Barents SRS operational area shall submit a report when entering into the area or on departure from a port or anchorage within the operational area.

3.4.1 ... or on departure from a port or anchorage within the operational area. 3.4.3 Ships departing a port or leaving an anchorage within the Barents SRS area, may also submit a pre-entry report for designators H, P, T, Q and X if transmitted one hour prior to departure.

Note: The master of the ship must forthwith inform the Barents SRS VTS centre concerned of any change in navigational status or in previous information notified, particularly in relation to designator Q.
4.1 Ships in the Barents SRS area are required to keep a continuous listening watch on VHF channel 16.

when.x: 3.5.2 Previously forwarded reports can be submitted at any time after entering the Danish Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) and until in reach of VHF range of Great Belt VTS at an approximate distance of 20 NM from the BELTREP area. As the Great Belt VTS must be able to timely handle incoming prior reporting, it will not be possible to undertake pre-entry reports within the 20 NM VHF range. The reporting option is then verbal reporting by VHF when crossing the report line of entry.

3.5.1 Ships entering the BELTREP operational area shall submit a report when crossing the report line or on departure from a port or anchorage within the operational area. 3.1.4 ... must, as a minimum, carry out a VHF voice transmission to communicate the name of the ship (part of designator A), air draught and deadweight tonnage (designator U) and the report line of entry to the Great Belt VTS when actually entering the area.

3.5.1 ... or on departure from a port or anchorage within the operational area. 3.5.3 Ships departing a port or leaving an anchorage within the 20 NM range of the BELTREP area or in the BELTREP area, may submit a pre-entry report for designators H, L, P, T and X if transmitted one hour before departure for enabling the Great Belt VTS to timely handle incoming prior reports.

Note a) The master of the ship must forthwith inform the Great Belt VTS concerned of any change in navigational status or in previous information notified, particularly in relation to designator Q or R. 3.1.5 Designator Q or R, if applicable, shall at all times be given using VHF voice transmission to Great Belt VTS.
3.2 Verbal reporting is not required when a ship passes the BELTREP sector line at latitude 55° 35′.00 N. However, sector change of VHF frequency is required according to appendix 2.

The lines were compared with the chartlet in Rev.1 appendix 1-A: RW runs from Korshavn on Fyn north to Samsø, RN from Samsø to the sea near Marthe Flak and east to Sjællands Odde, RS from Stigsnæs over Omø and the sea to Langeland's east coast, RSW from Langeland's west coast to the Thurø Rev light buoy; the coast closes the rest. A text diff of MSC.332(90) and Rev.1 showed the only changes of substance are the insurance certificates added to X and in 3.1.3, the liability note in 9.3 (action on missing liability certificates only if the flag State is party to the Conventions), and the revocation of MSC.63(67) annex 1 and MSC.332(90) from 1 December 2026. nt: From 0000 UTC 1 December 2026 MSC.332(90)/Rev.1 replaces MSC.332(90) and annex 1 of MSC.63(67); boundary, ships, channels and phone stay the same, and line X then also asks for the insurance / civil liability certificates (CLC 1992, Bunkers 2001, Nairobi WRC 2007); the company may give the certificate information (SOLAS IX/1.2). E-mail: the IMO texts print beltrep@sok.dk, the Danish Defence page (2024) gives vts@beltrep.org; use the web page address first and confirm by VHF or phone if unsure. Point 10 is a light buoy at sea, not a coast point: the RSW line is drawn only between points 9 and 10, so the short gap from the buoy to Thurø is not printed. Pre-entry non-verbal reports are possible only from entering the Danish EEZ until about 20 NM from the area (chartlet in appendix 1-B); inside 20 NM report by VHF at the report line. Bridges: West Bridge spans only for ships under 1,000 dwt and air draught under 18.00 m (route BW); East Bridge for air draught under 65.00 m (route BE, route T); recommended speed limit 20 knots in TSS Korsoer - Sprogoe. Ships with draught 11 m or more on route T, and INF cargo ships, are recommended to take a pilot (IMO Recommendation on navigation through the entrances to the Baltic Sea). National order: BEK nr. 820 af 26/06/2013 (BELTREP), named on the Danish Defence page. History: first adopted by MSC.63(67) annex 1 (in force 3 June 1997), amended by A.978(24) (1 July 2006) and MSC.230(82) (1 July 2007), then MSC.332(90) (1 July 2013).

ver: Text extracted from the IMO PDF of MSC.73(69) (pdftotext). Every coordinate digit checked against the rendered PDF pages 14 and 16 (annex pages 13 and 15) at 120 dpi; the report letters checked against page 17 (annex page 16); categories and area against page 13 (annex page 12). Amendments: the IMO index pages of MSC resolutions from 1997-99 to 2026-27 (read 2026-10-26) list no amendment of BONIFREP; the Swedish 2026 SRS list also cites only MSC.73(69). The VHF call and channel 10 are repeated in IMO MEPC.204(62) (2011). I found no current French (premar-mediterranee.gouv.fr) or Italian (guardiacostiera.gov.it) web page on BONIFREP to confirm the channels today. The circle centre is not printed and was taken as Bonifacio town (inferred).
nt: Area: the resolution only says "a circular area with a radius of 20 (twenty) nautical miles centred on Bonifacio"; it prints no centre position. The centre here (41 23.3N 009 09.6E, Bonifacio town) is an assumption (inferred), so the circle edge is approximate. The report itself is tied to the reporting lines and the precautionary areas at each end of the two way route, not to the circle. The four points given are the sea ends of the reporting lines as printed; the land ends are beacons (Cap De Fano, Capo Testa, Pointe De Rondinara, Punta Galera) whose positions are not printed, so they are not given. IMO A.766(18) still asks flag States to prohibit or strongly discourage transit by laden oil tankers and ships carrying dangerous chemicals or substances in bulk; French and Italian flag ships carrying oil or hazardous goods are banned from the Strait (MSC.73(69) para 6.4). Since 2011 the Strait is a PSSA (MEPC.204(62)): pilotage is recommended for those ships; vessels ordering a pilot confirm ETA 2 hours before arrival by calling "Bonifacio Traffic" on VHF 10; pilot boarding positions (WGS 84) 41° 24'.80 N 009° 30'.00 E (east) and 41° 17'.28 N 008° 58'.50 E (west). French national rules (Prefet maritime arrete n° 84/98, amended by 56/2003, and the older arrete n° 23/83 with a 6 hour notice for hazardous cargo entering French territorial waters, as described in MSC.73(69) para 6.3) are national and not covered here; see the SURNAV records. The 1998 text says an IMO circular could give another back up channel after 1 February 1999; I found none. Not confirmed on a current French or Italian official web page.

when.x: North-east bound traffic should report to GRIS NEZ TRAFFIC on the French coast 2 nautical miles before crossing the line from the Royal Sovereign light tower, through the Bassurelle Light Buoy (at its assigned position of 50°32'.8N, 000°57'.8E) to the coast of France.

South-west-bound traffic should report to the shore at DOVER COASTGUARD on the English coast when within VHF range of North Foreland and not later when crossing the line drawn from North Foreland to the border between France and Belgium.

Reports to the nearer of the two shore stations should be made on departure from a port within the coverage area. Recognizing that cross-Channel ferries generally operate according to published schedules, special reporting arrangements can be made on a ship-by-ship basis, subject to the approval of both GRIS NEZ TRAFFIC and DOVER COASTGUARD.
Further reports should be made to the relevant shore station whenever there is a change of navigational circumstance, particularly in relation to items Q and R of the reporting format.

t: CANREP Canary Islands
au: MRCC Las Palmas and MRCC Tenerife (Salvamento Maritimo)
ap: Tankers of 600 tonnes deadweight and upwards carrying heavy crude oil, heavy fuel oil, or bitumen and tar and their emulsions, whether transiting, going to or from Canarian ports, or sailing between the islands.
apq: 1.1 Ships required to take part in the CANREP system: Tankers of 600 tonnes deadweight and upwards, either transiting the Canary Islands or sailing to or from Canarian ports or involved in inter-island navigation, carrying the following: .1 heavy-grade crude oils with a density greater than 900 kg/m³ at 15°C; .2 heavy fuel oils with a density greater than 900 kg/m³ at 15°C or kinematic viscosity greater than 180 mm²/s at 50°C; and .3 bitumen, coal tar and their emulsions.

when.x: 3.3.1 Ships must submit a report: .1 on entering the reporting area as defined in paragraph 2. Appendix 2, para 7: The sailing plan (SP) is sent as an initial report: (a) When entering the reporting area, as defined in paragraph 2.1.
.2 immediately after leaving a port, terminal or anchorage situated in the reporting area. Appendix 2, para 7: (b) On leaving the last port of call located in the reporting area.
.3 when deviating from the route leading to the originally declared destination, port, terminal, anchorage or position "for orders" given on entry into the reporting area
.4 when it is necessary to deviate from the planned route owing to weather conditions, damaged equipment or a change in navigational status
.5 on finally leaving the reporting area. Appendix 2, para 8: The final report (FR) is sent: (a) When leaving the reporting area.
Appendix 2, para 8: The final report (FR) is sent: (b) On arrival at a port of destination located in the reporting area.
3.3.2 Ships are not required to send a report if, during normal sailing through the reporting area, they cross the area's boundary on other occasions apart from initial entry or final departure.

Date and time corresponding to position at C, expressed as UTC: A six-digit group followed by a Z. The first two digits indicate day of the month, the second two the hours and the last two the minutes. The Z indicates that the time is given in UTC (e.g., 081340Z).

Position (latitude and longitude): A 4-digit group giving latitude in degrees and minutes, with the suffix N, and a 5-digit group giving longitude in degrees and minutes, with the suffix W (e.g., 2836N or 01545W).
Course: True course. A 3-digit group (e.g., 210).
Speed: Speed in knots. A 2-digit group (e.g.,14).
Name of last port of call: Name of the last port of call (e.g., Strait of Gibraltar)
Destination and ETA (UTC): Name of destination and date and time group as expressed in B (e.g., Cape Town 181400Z)
Cargo: Type(s) of cargo, and quantity and IMO classification if carrying potentially dangerous goods.
Defects, damage, deficiencies, limitations: Brief details of defects, including damage, deficiencies and other circumstances that impair normal navigation.
Address for the communication of cargo information: Name, tel No. and fax, e-mail or URL.
Total number of people on board: State number

Miscellaneous: Miscellaneous information concerning those tankers: Characteristics and approximate quantity of bunker fuel for tankers carrying an amount of it greater than 5,000 tonnes. Navigational status (e.g., moving under own propulsion, at anchor, no steering, limited manoeuvrability, depth restriction, moored, aground, etc.)

fn: Every report begins with the word CANREP and a two-letter type: SP (sailing plan), FR (final report), DR (deviation report). Messages with this prefix are free of charge and treated as URGENT. Compulsory lines (Appendix 2, para 6): SP: A, B, C, E, F, G, I, P, T, W and X. FR: A, B, C, E and F. DR: A, B, C, E, F and I. Q is added whenever a problem arises that affects normal navigation. The req values above are for the sailing plan. Format follows resolution A.851(20). Note: in the source, the deviation report example is headed "CANREP - FR"; it is a misprint for DR (para 9). Report on exit to the same MRCC as on entry (para 3.4.2).

t: COPREP Off the coast of Portugal
au: ROCA CONTROL (Portuguese coastal VTS, Centro de Controlo de Trafego Maritimo do Continente, DGRM)
ap: Ships of 300 GT and above; all ships with dangerous, hazardous or potentially polluting cargo; all passenger ships; towing or pushing units over 100 m combined; fishing vessels of 24 m LOA or more. Others are invited to report voluntarily.
apq: The following vessels are required to participate in the COPREP System: (a) all vessels of 300 gross tonnage or above; (b) all vessels carrying dangerous, hazardous and/or potentially polluting cargo; (c) all passenger vessels; (d) vessels engaged in towing or pushing where the combined length of the vessel and tow or pushed vessel is more than 100 m LOA; (e) fishing vessels with an LOA of 24 m or above; and (f) any other type of vessel is invited to voluntarily participate in the System.

when.x: 3.3.1 Ships must submit a report: (a) on entering the reporting area as defined in paragraph 2.1
(b) immediately after leaving a port, terminal or anchorage situated in the reporting area
(c) when deviating from the route leading to the originally declared destination, port, terminal, anchorage or position "for orders" given on entry into the reporting area
(d) when it is necessary to deviate from the planned route owing to weather conditions, damaged equipment or a change in navigational status
(e) when something is detected that could affect safety of navigation in the area
(f) on finally leaving the reporting area
(g) when requested by COPREP operator.

3.3.2 Ships who have submitted a voluntary report with the same designator letters prior to entering the reporting area are only required to submit a mandatory report: (a) if there are any changes in previously submitted information; (b) with designator letters "A" and "H" when entering the reporting area.

apq: Ships of the following general categories are required to participate in the reporting system: .1 All ships of 50 metres or more in length overall. .2 All ships, regardless of length, carrying hazardous and or potentially polluting cargo, as defined in paragraph 1.4 of resolution MSC.43(64). .3 Ships engaged in towing or pushing another vessel where the combined length of the ship and tow or pushed vessel exceeds 50 metres. .4 Any category of vessel less than 50 metres in length overall which is using the appropriate traffic lane or separation zone in order to engage in fishing. .5 Any category of ships less than 50 metres in length overall which is using the appropriate traffic lane or separation zone in an emergency in order to avoid immediate danger.

t: GDANREP Approaches to the Polish ports in the Gulf of Gdansk
au: Director of the Maritime Office in Gdynia; reports to VTS Centre Gulf of Gdansk (voice call sign VTS Zatoka)
ap: All passenger ships, ships of 150 GT and above, and all vessels engaged in towing, going to or from Polish ports or passing through the area between Polish ports in the Gulf of Gdansk, or visiting the area.
apq: 1.1 Ships of the following categories are required to participate in the system proceeding to or from Polish ports or passing through the reporting area between Polish ports in the Gulf of Gdańsk, or ships visiting the area: - all passenger ships as defined in Chapter 1 of 1974 SOLAS, as amended; - ships of 150 gross tonnage and above; - all vessels engaged in towing.

when.x: 3.3.1 The ship shall transmit the Sailing Plan (SP) on entry into the ship reporting system area by crossing Reporting Line.
3.3.2 The ship shall transmit the Position Report (PR) on passing the Reporting Points.
3.3.3 The ship shall transmit the Final Report (FR) when finally exiting from the ship reporting system area by crossing Reporting Line.

3.3.4 In the case of incidents or accidents as described in paragraph 3.2.4 the ship(s) shall transmit the Other Report(s) immediately to the shore-based Authority. The vessel(s) shall provide any additional information related to the incident or accident as requested by the shore-based Authority.

src.t: IMO MSC.249(83) Adoption of a new mandatory ship reporting system on the approaches to the Polish ports in the Gulf of Gdansk (GDANREP)

ver: Reporting Line points (1)-(4) and Reporting Points (5), (6), (8)-(12) were taken from the text layer of MSC.249(83) Annex page 2 (PDF page 3) and every digit was checked against a 150 dpi render of the page. The Maritime Office in Gdynia VTS page prints the same four Reporting Line positions as the outer limit of VTS Zatoka Gdanska. Point (1) lies on the Hel Peninsula where it meets parallel 54 45N and point (4) on the Vistula Spit near the Polish / Russian border, so the line closes the gulf from coast to coast; the coast closes the rest. Rules and report contents: MSC.249(83), no later IMO amendment found in the IMO index of MSC resolutions (read 2026-10-26). Channel 71 and phone, e-mail and fax: Maritime Office in Gdynia web page, read 2026-10-26.
nt: Reporting Point (7) is not printed in the resolution: the list goes (5), (6), (8), (9) ... and is copied as printed. The reporting points are given for the Position Report and are not part of the boundary. The area is Polish territorial and internal waters south of 54 45N, so Puck Bay north of 54 45N is outside. The resolution does not say when a ship leaving a Polish port gives its Sailing Plan; it only says SP on entry by crossing the Reporting Line and FR when finally exiting. The Maritime Office page (2024) says all ships entering or in the VTS area must use the VTS reporting system under Order No 11 of the Director of the Maritime Office in Gdynia of 17 May 2023 (VTS regulations), and that the ships listed in GDANREP may not enter the VTS area, or leave a berth or anchorage in it, without a traffic clearance from VTS; check that order for the national details. Inside the ports and roads of Gdynia and Gdansk the harbour master's traffic services act as VTS. Separate from GDANREP: VTS Lawica Slupska (Slupsk Bank TSS) uses VHF 73 and vtslawica@umgdy.gov.pl (Maritime Office page, 2025); it is a national VTS, not an IMO ship reporting system.

t: GIBREP Strait of Gibraltar
au: MRCC Tarifa (TARIFA TRAFFIC, Salvamento Maritimo, Spain) and CSTM Tanger (TANGIER TRAFFIC, Morocco)
res: MSC.63(67) Annex 2, as amended by MSC.300(87)
ap: Ships of 300 GT and over; any ship with hazardous or potentially polluting cargo; any ship towing or pushing; ships under 300 GT using the traffic lanes or separation zone to fish or in an emergency. Regular cross-Strait ferries can have special arrangements.
apq: 1.1 Ships of the following general categories are required to participate in the reporting system: .1 all ships of 300 gross tonnage and over; .2 all ships, regardless of gross tonnage, carrying hazardous and/or potentially polluting cargo, as defined in paragraph 1.4 of the Guidelines and criteria for ship reporting systems (resolution MSC.43(64)); .3 ships engaged in towing or pushing another vessel regardless of gross tonnage; .4 any category of vessel less than 300 gross tonnage which is using the appropriate traffic lane or separation zone in order to engage in fishing; and .5 any category of ships less than 300 gross tonnage which is using the appropriate traffic separation zone in an emergency in order to avoid immediate danger. Exemption 1.2 Recognizing that regular cross-Strait ferries, including passenger high-speed craft, generally operate according to published schedules, special reporting arrangements can be made on a ship-by-ship basis, subject to the approval of both TARIFA TRAFFIC and TANGIER TRAFFIC.

when.x: 3.3.1 Westbound traffic should report to TARIFA TRAFFIC on the Spanish coast when crossing the meridian 005°15'.00 W (appendix).
3.3.2 Eastbound traffic should report to TANGIER TRAFFIC on the Moroccan coast when crossing the meridian 005° 58'.00 W (appendix).

3.3.3 Reports to the nearer of the two shore stations should be made on departure from the limits of a port or anchorage within the coverage area, except vessels departing from Tangier-Med ports and its anchorage areas which should report to TANGIER TRAFFIC (appendix).

3.3.4 Further reports should be made to the relevant shore station whenever there is a change of navigational circumstances, particularly in relation to items Q and R of the reporting format detailed in section 3.2.

src.t: IMO MSC.300(87) Adoption of amendments to the existing mandatory ship reporting system In the Strait of Gibraltar (GIBREP)
IMO MSC.63(67) Mandatory ship reporting systems, Annex 2 In the Strait of Gibraltar

ver: All rules, lines and contacts from MSC.300(87) Annex: every page rendered at 120 dpi and read against the extracted text (pages 2 to 7); the IMO PDF has no appendix chartlet. The reporting meridians 005 58W and 005 15W also appear on the 1996 chartlet of MSC.63(67) Appendix 1 (rendered and read). The four coast points are NOT printed: they were computed where each meridian meets the Natural Earth 10m land outline (accuracy a few hundred metres) and are only for drawing. Salvamento Maritimo web page (read 2026-10-26) confirms CCS Tarifa provides the traffic service in the Strait and the mandatory reporting system; it lists no VHF channel. The Moroccan authority sites (dmm.gov.ma, equipement.gov.ma) did not answer on 2026-10-26.
nt: The boundary is two meridians, 005 58W (west) and 005 15W (east), from coast to coast; the coast points are inferred COAST POINTs. Westbound ships report to TARIFA TRAFFIC at 005 15W; eastbound ships report to TANGIER TRAFFIC at 005 58W. Ships leaving a port or anchorage inside the area report to the nearer station, but from Tangier-Med always to TANGIER TRAFFIC. MSC.300(87) (in force 1 December 2010) replaced the 1996 text: before that the threshold was 50 m LOA and all reports went to Tarifa on VHF 16 and 10 (67 supplementary). Broadcasts: Tarifa on VHF 10 at 00:15, 04:15, 08:15, 12:15, 16:15, 20:15 UTC; Tangier on VHF 69 at 02:15, 06:15, 10:15, 14:15, 18:15, 22:15 UTC, each announced on VHF 16 (MSC.300(87) para 3.5.2). Email, fax and Inmarsat telex are as printed in 2010 and were not reconfirmed on current official pages. Later amendments: none found. Checked the Swedish Transport Agency list of IMO ship reporting systems (2017), the NCSR 12 report to MSC (NCSR 12/20/Add.1, 2025), the MSC 111 summary (May 2026: only ADRIREP, SOUNDREP, BELTREP were adopted) and the NCSR 13 draft report (NCSR 13/WP.1/Rev.1: proposals only for TRANSREP, BONIFREP, WETREP, CALDOVREP). An EU proposal at NCSR 12 to add insurance certificate lines to about ten European systems is still being handled at IMO; if it reaches this system the report lines will change.

t: GOFREP Gulf of Finland mandatory ship reporting system
au: Helsinki Traffic (Fintraffic, Gulf of Finland VTS Centre, Finland); Tallinn Traffic (Estonian Transport Administration, Tallinn VTS Centre); St. Petersburg Traffic (Russian Federation)
res: MSC.139(76) annex 1, as amended by MSC.231(82)
ap: Ships of 300 GT and over. Ships under 300 GT should report when not under command or at anchor in a TSS, restricted in their ability to manoeuvre, or with defective navigational aids.
apq: 1.1 Ships of 300 gross tonnage and over are required to participate in the mandatory ship reporting system. Ships under 300 gross tonnage should make reports in circumstances where they: .1 are not under command or at anchor in the TSS; .2 are restricted in their ability to manoeuvre; and .3 have defective navigational aids.

when.x: Full Report: Vessels not equipped with AIS entering the GOFREP area from the Northern Baltic or Väinameri, are recommended to give a Full Report to the relevant Traffic Centre by fax or e-mail at least one hour before entering the area. In any case, a Full Report shall be given prior to entering the GOFREP area.
Full Report: 3.3.2 Ships shall submit a Full Report: 1. when entering the GOFREP area from the west or from Väinameri,

Full Report: 3.3.2 Ships shall submit a Full Report: ... 2. on departure from a port or latest before entering the reporting area, 3. on departure from a port if it shall not enter the reporting area at all, 4. before departing from Russian Port areas. A Full Report on departure from a port is given to the Traffic Centre of the country whose port the vessel is departing in the Gulf of Finland traffic area.

Short Report: 3.3.4 Ships shall submit a Short Report: 1. on entering the GOFREP area from the Estonian or Finnish VTS areas in the Gulf of Finland, 2. on crossing the Western or Väinameri Reporting Line inward-bound to Gulf of Finland,

Short Report: 3.3.4 Ships shall submit a Short Report: ... 3. on crossing the Central Reporting Line, ... Short Report is given on VHF when crossing the Central Reporting Line to the Traffic Centre of the country to which monitoring area the vessel is proceeding.
Short Report: 3.3.4 Ships shall submit a Short Report: ... 4. whenever there is a change in the vessel's navigational status excluding the change of status when berthing or unberthing.

If there are any circumstances affecting normal navigation in accordance with the provisions of the SOLAS and MARPOL Conventions, the Master of the vessel in question is obliged to report designator Q or R, whichever is relevant under the prevailing circumstances. This report shall be made without delay.

ver: Boundary: the 50 points were taken from the text layer of MSC.231(82) Annex page 3 (PDF page 4) and every digit was checked against a 170 dpi render of that page; point 50 is printed with one decimal of a minute (59° 10′.0 N) and is kept so. The ring 1 to 50 and back to 1 is closed by the Western Reporting Line (50 to 1); the points run along the Finnish side (1 to 23), back west along the Russian side (24 to 33) and along the Estonian side (34 to 49), and lie at sea. Rules, report contents and VHF channels: MSC.231(82) Annex (in force 1 July 2007), with the unamended parts of MSC.139(76) Annex 1. E-mail and phone numbers: not printed in either IMO text; taken from the live Fintraffic Master's Guide web page and the 2021 PDF (same numbers). The IMO index of MSC resolutions (pages 2000-03 to 2026-27, read 2026-10-26) shows no later amendment or revision of GOFREP.
nt: One record, not one per centre: the IMO text gives one outer boundary and the same rules for all three centres; the three monitoring areas are split by the Central Reporting Line, whose western part is defined in the IMO text only as the midpoints of the separation zones of the TSS off Kõpu, Hankoniemi, Porkkala and Kalbådagrund to 59° 59′.15 N 026° 30′.00 E, so separate sector boundaries could not be drawn from the IMO text without inventing points. Which centre to call: north of the Central Reporting Line Helsinki Traffic; south of it and west of 026 30E (or from Väinameri) Tallinn Traffic; south of it and east of 026 30E St. Petersburg Traffic. When crossing the Central Reporting Line, report to the centre whose area you are entering; you need not report to the centre you are leaving (Fintraffic). Eastern part of the Central Reporting Line (MSC.231(82) 3.3.1): 59° 57′.0 N 026° 30′.00 E to 60° 05′.00 N 026° 30′.00 E, then along the Russian territorial sea / Finnish EEZ limit to 60° 08′.90 N 026° 49′.00 E, then along the Finland / Russia EEZ limit to 60° 10′.30 N 026° 57′.50 E, to 60° 10′.30 N 027° 10′.90 E and to 60° 12′.00 N 027° 17′.60 E. The Fintraffic Master's Guide also lists 17 points of the western part (59°05,88'N 021°40,08'E to 59°59,15'N 026°30,00'E), the Väinameri reporting line (59º06,00'N 022º35,00'E to 59º14,00'N 023º31,00'E) and the outer limits of the Finnish and Tallinn VTS areas; these are national data, not IMO text, and are not drawn here. The polygon leaves out the Finnish and Estonian VTS areas and Russian territorial waters, which have their own national VTS reporting. Ships in an icebreaker convoy need not give a Short Report at the reporting lines; the icebreaker reports them (Fintraffic). History: the 2004 system (MSC.139(76), from 1 July 2004) covered international waters only, between the Bengtskär - 59°33'.30 N 022°30'E - 59°10'N 021°30'E - Kõpu line and 026°30'E, with different report letters; MSC.231(82) replaced the boundary, the report letters and the reporting points from 1 July 2007. Contact details for Tallinn and St. Petersburg Traffic come only from the Finnish Master's Guide; they could not be confirmed on Estonian or Russian official pages. Participation of the Russian centre since 2022 was not checked against a Russian source; Fintraffic still lists St. Petersburg Traffic (page read 2026-10-26).

t: MANCHEREP Off Les Casquets and the adjacent coastal area
au: CROSS Jobourg, VTS call sign Jobourg Traffic (printed 'Jobourg Trafic')
ap: Ships of over 300 GT. Ships under 300 GT keep reporting under the voluntary MAREP scheme when not under command or at anchor in the TSS or coastal area, restricted in their ability to manoeuvre, or with defective aids to navigation.
apq: The new system will apply to ships of over 300 GT, in line with the MAREP, OUESSREP and CALDOVREP systems already in place in the Channel or west of the Channel.

when.x: The call should be made 2 nautical miles before entering the area (chart annexed).

Ships making regular voyages from a port situated within the coverage area or in an adjacent area must send their reports to Jobourg. However, since ferries generally sail in accordance with fixed schedules, it will be possible for arrangements to be made on a case-by-case basis between ships and the Jobourg VTS.
A ship may elect, for reasons of commercial confidentiality, to communicate that section of the report which provides information on cargo by non-verbal means prior to entering the system.

t: TRANSREP off the south and south-west coast of Iceland
au: Icelandic Maritime Traffic Service (MTS), Reykjavik, operated by the Icelandic Coast Guard
ap: Ships calling at ports inside the eastern ATBA off the south and south-west coast of Iceland; ships under 5,000 GT allowed to transit the eastern ATBA south of 63 45N on voyages between Icelandic ports without dangerous or noxious bulk cargo; ships up to 20,000 GT to or from Faxaflói Bay without dangerous goods or noxious bulk cargo that may transit the eastern ATBA south of 63 45N; passenger ships of any size, which may only transit the inner route (Húllid Passage) and the eastern ATBA from 1 May to 1 October. Not for government ships, fishing vessels with fishing rights in Iceland's EEZ, or research vessels.
apq: 1.1 Ships of the following categories are required to participate in the system: .1 ships calling at ports located within the eastern ATBA off the south and southwest coast of Iceland; and .2 ships of less than 5,000 gross tonnage permitted to transit the eastern ATBA south of latitude 63° 45' N when engaged on voyages between Icelandic ports and not carrying dangerous or noxious cargoes in bulk or in cargo tanks. [added by MSC.316(88):] .3 ships of up to 20,000 gross tonnage, en route to or from Faxaflói Bay, which neither carry dangerous goods nor noxious materials in bulk or cargo tanks and which may transit the Eastern ATBA south of latitude 63° 45' N; and .4 passenger ships of unlimited size, which may only transit the inner route (Húllid Passage) and the Eastern ATBA during the period 1 May to 1 October. [MSC.250(83):] Pursuant to SOLAS 1974, the mandatory ship reporting system does not apply to any warship, naval auxiliary, coast guard vessel, or other vessel owned or operated by a contracting government and used, for the time being, only on government non-commercial service. However, such ships are encouraged to participate in the reporting system. The mandatory ship reporting system does not apply to fishing vessels with fishing rights within Iceland's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and research vessels.

nt: The area is the eastern ATBA as defined in the 2007 text. Points 1 and 20 longitudes are not printed (UK coast); their values here are read off a map and marked inferred. Portugal e-mail taken from the DGRM page via the COPREP record (same day). Other centre details are only as printed in 2004; not reconfirmed on current national pages.
nt: Boundary: the official boundary is the line 1 to 18 (from the east coast of Caithness out to 62N, down the west of Ireland, the zigzag 7-8-9-10-11 west of Brittany and in the Bay of Biscay, then down to the Guadiana mouth), plus three closing lines: 19-20 across the southern North Sea (Belgium/Netherlands border to Suffolk), 21-22 across the south of St George's Channel and 23-24 across the North Channel. The rest is the coast. So the Irish Sea, the North Sea north of 52 12N and the outer Bay of Biscay are NOT in the area, but the English Channel is. Point 1 (58 30N on the UK coast) and point 20 (52 12N on the UK east coast) have no printed longitude; 003 06W and 001 37E are approximate coast positions (inferred). Points 21 to 24 are printed in MSC.190(79) as e.g. 52° 01'.52" (stray quote marks); MEPC.121(52) prints the same points as 52°01.52'N, so they are decimal minutes. Points 6 and 7: MSC.190(79) prints 54° 40'40".91 N and 50° 56'45".36 N; MEPC.121(52) prints 54°40'40.9"N and 50°56'45.3"N (point 7 differs by 0.06 seconds; MSC.190(79) is used here). The centre list is from 2004 (Portugal from 2010) and is out of date in places (UK coastguard reorganisation, old e-mail domains): use the current list in official national publications and confirm the address on first contact. Points 8 and 10 are labelled (Irl+UK+F) and (F+S) in the source: they mark where the national parts meet. Ships bound to or from a port in the area must also meet EU Directive 2002/59/EC (footnote to para 6.2). No amendment after MSC.301(87) found in the IMO index of MSC resolutions up to MSC 111 (May 2026) or in the Swedish Transport Agency list of 2026.

t: Galapagos PSSA mandatory ship reporting system (GALREP)
au: Santa Cruz Maritime Rescue Sub-Centre (MRSC Puerto Ayora) via Puerto Ayora Radio (HCY); alternate Baquerizo Moreno Radio (HCW). National maritime authority: DIRNEA (formerly DIGMER).
ap: All ships.
apq: All ships are required to participate in the mandatory ship reporting system. (MSC.229(82), Annex, para 1.1)

when.x: A ship must give a full report at the following positions: .1 on entering the reporting area; (para 3.4.1)
.2 immediately after leaving a port or anchorage located in the Galapagos PSSA (the co-ordinates of which are at appendix 4); (para 3.4.1)

.3 when deviating from the route leading to the port of destination or anchorage reported originally; .4 when it is necessary to deviate from the planned route owing to weather conditions, damaged equipment or a change in navigational status; (para 3.4.1)
.5 on finally leaving the reporting area. (para 3.4.1) Final report: FR (on finally leaving reporting area) to include only A, B, C, E and F. (appendix 3)

ln.x: Ship: Name and call sign (Name of ship, call sign, IMO No. and MMSI No.), (e.g., TAURUS/HC4019/T-04-0561)
Date and time corresponding to position at C, expressed as UTC: a six-digit group followed by a Z (e.g., 081340Z).

Position (latitude and longitude): a 4-digit group giving latitude in degrees and minutes, with the suffix N or S, and a 5-digit group giving longitude in degrees and minutes, with the suffix W (e.g., 0030S 08805W).
Course: true course. A 3-digit group (e.g., 270).
Speed: speed in knots. A 2-digit group (e.g., 14).
Name of last port of call (e.g., Guayaquil). Sailing plan only.
Destination and ETA (UTC): name of destination and date and time group as expressed in B (e.g., Puerto Ayora 082200Z). Sailing plan and deviation report.

Cargo: type(s) of oil cargo, quantity, quality and density of heavy crude, heavy fuel, asphalt and coal tar. If the ships are carrying other potentially hazardous cargoes, indicate type, quantity and IMO classification (e.g., 10,000 TN DIESEL OIL). Sailing plan only.

Defects, damage, deficiencies, limitations: brief details of defects, including damage, deficiencies and other circumstances that impair normal navigation. Included whenever a problem arises in the reporting area.
Address for the communication of cargo information: name, telephone no., and either fax or e-mail. Sailing plan only.
Total no. of people on board: state how many. Sailing plan only.

Miscellaneous: characteristics and approximate quantity of bunker fuel for tankers carrying an amount of it greater than 5,000 tonnes; navigational status (e.g., at anchor, moving under own propulsion, no steering, limited manoeuvrability, depth restriction, moored, aground, etc.). Sailing plan only.

fn: Every message must begin with the word GALREP and the two-letter report type: SP sailing plan, FR final report, DR deviation report (messages with these prefixes are free of charge). SP: A, B, C, E, F, G, I, P, T, W and X are compulsory. FR: only A, B, C, E and F. DR: only A, B, C, E, F and I. Q is added whenever a defect or problem arises. Language: Spanish or English, IMO SMCP where necessary. Commercially confidential information may be sent by non-verbal means.
aq: The operational area of GALREP covers the Galapagos Area to be Avoided and the Particularly Sensitive Sea Area as shown on the chartlet given in appendix 1. The reference chart is I.O.A 20 (2nd edition 1992, updated and reprinted in 2006), issued by the Ecuadorean Navy Oceanography Institute (INOCAR), based on WGS 84 Datum. (MSC.229(82), Annex, paras 2.1, 2.1.1, 2.2)

nt: Boundary: high confidence (straight lines between the 12 printed points, WGS 84). The PSSA points in appendix 4 (A to L, a smaller polygon) are the PSSA limit, not the reporting area. Contacts: low confidence. Every email, phone, fax and Inmarsat number here is copied from the 2006 resolution; none was confirmed current (the islasantacruz.com and digmer.org domains and the Inmarsat Mini-M service are likely obsolete). Before entering, check the current Ecuadorian notices (DIRNEA, INOCAR) or the local agent. Ships must keep a continuous listening watch in the area. Ships must also respect the Galapagos Area to be Avoided (IMO) and Ecuador's own rules for entering the Galapagos Marine Reserve, which this record does not cover.

t: Greenland ship reporting system GREENPOS (ships on voyage to and from Greenland)
au: Joint Arctic Command / JRCC Greenland, Nuuk (formerly Island Commander Greenland / MRCC Grønnedal)
ap: All ships on voyage to or from Greenland ports and places of call, while within the continental shelf or exclusive economic zone of Greenland.
apq: Ships required to participate in the reporting system GREENPOS: All ships, on voyage to or from Greenland ports and places of call. (MSC.126(75), Annex, para 1.1)

when.x: Sailing Plan ("SP") to be sent as a first report: a. When entering the reporting area (Appendix 1, para 5)
b. On last departure from Greenland port (Appendix 1, para 5)
Position Report ("PR") to be sent 4 times a day: At 0000-0030Z, 0600-0630Z, 1200-1230Z and 1800-1830Z. (Appendix 1, para 6)

Deviation Report ("DR") to be sent: When the position of the ship is or will be changed considerably compared with the position, at which the ship, based on former reports, is expected to be. (Appendix 1, para 8)
Final Report ("FR") to be sent: a. When leaving the reporting area. b. On arrival at Greenland destination. (Appendix 1, para 7)

how.n: Contact published by Danish Defence for JRCC Greenland (page updated 2021). The IMO text and the 2003 Order send GREENPOS reports to Island Command Greenland via Naval Radio Grønnedal (OVC/GLK), which has since moved to Joint Arctic Command in Nuuk; no official page found that names this address for GREENPOS reports. Confirm before use.
As published by Danish Defence (2021).

how.v: via a Greenland coast radio station
how.n: The rules allow reports via a coast radio station (Appendix 1, para 2). The 2182 kHz watch at Grønnedal named in the 2002 and 2003 texts is not confirmed current.

ad: GLK GROENNEDAL (as in the 2002 IMO examples; now Joint Arctic Command)

ln.x: Ship: name and call sign (e.g.: AGNETHE NIELSEN/OULH). All reports.
Date Time Group corresponding to the position under designator C or D, given in UTC: a 6-digit group followed by a Z (e.g.: 041330Z). All reports.

Position by latitude and longitude: a 4-digit group giving latitude in degrees and minutes suffixed with N, and a 5-digit group giving longitude in degrees and minutes suffixed with W (e.g.: 5710N 04112W). C or D for all reports.

Position by geographical name of place: name of place or true bearing (3 digits) and distance in nautical miles (quote the word distance) from an unambiguous known name of place (e.g.: 165 distance 53 Cape Farewell). Instead of C.
True course: a 3-digit group (e.g.: 083). SP and PR.
Speed in knots: a 2-digit group (e.g.: 14). SP and PR.
Destination and ETA (UTC): name of the destination followed by expected time of arrival as under B (e.g.: Nanortalik 181400Z). SP.
Intended voyage: a brief description of the intended route, as estimated by the Master. SP (and DR).
Defects and deficiencies: brief details of defects and deficiencies of significance for the safety of the ship (e.g.: Breakdown on Radar and VHF).
Weather and ice conditions: brief information about weather at the time of the report and about the ice situation since the last report (e.g.: SW 5, ice edge observed from 6120N03905W). All reports.
The total number of persons on board (e.g.: POB 16) and other relevant information of importance to the safety of own or other ships. SP.

fn: Each report begins with the word GREENPOS and a 2-letter type: SP sailing plan, PR position report, FR final report, DR deviation report; reports so prefixed are free of charge and carry priority URGENT. SP: A, B, C or D, E, F, I, L, S, X. PR: A, B, C or D, E, F, S. FR: A, B, C or D, S. DR: A, B, C or D and the changed items (example uses L). Times in UTC.

aq: The reporting system GREENPOS covers the area within the Continental Shelf or Exclusive Economic Zone off the coast of Greenland. The reference charts are Danish charts Nos. 1000 (Datum Qornoq 1927), 2000 and 3000 (Datum unknown). (MSC.126(75), Annex, paras 2.1 and 2.2)
