JRCC Greenland email and phone from the Danish Defence Joint Arctic Command web page (updated 4 May 2021). No IMO amendment to the Greenland system found in a scan of MSC resolutions 43 to 599.
nt: Rules (who, when, format): high confidence, unchanged since 2002/2003. Address: low confidence. The official texts still name Island Command Greenland / Naval Radio Grønnedal, which closed; the duties moved to Joint Arctic Command (Arktisk Kommando) in Nuuk, whose JRCC is responsible for GREENPOS. The email and phone given are JRCC Greenland's published contacts, not a published GREENPOS address. Confirm the current GREENPOS address (for example with JRCC Greenland or the Danish Maritime Authority) before the voyage. The area is Greenland's continental shelf or EEZ (no coordinates in the source). The second system in the same resolution, COASTAL CONTROL (KYSTKONTROL, ships of 20 GT and more and fishing vessels on voyages between Greenland ports, reports to the coast radio station of the destination area), is not in this record. Greenland lies outside geographical Europe, but is a Danish system: another record set may also list it.

t: Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument PSSA ship reporting system (CORAL SHIPREP), North-western Hawaiian Islands
au: United States Coast Guard Communication Area Master Station Pacific (CAMSPAC) as shore-based authority; reports go to NOAA (nwhi.notifications@noaa.gov)
ap: Ships of 300 gross tonnage or more in transit through the reporting area that are entering or leaving a United States port or place (condition of port entry), and all such ships in a developing emergency. Sovereign immune ships exempt. Other ships of 300 GT or more, fishing vessels and all ships in an emergency are recommended to report. US-flag vessels must report under US law.
apq: As a condition of entry to a United States port or place, all ships 300 gross tonnage or greater, and all ships in the event of a developing emergency, and that are in transit through the reporting area are required to participate in CORAL SHIPREP, except for sovereign immune vessels which are exempt under SOLAS regulation V/1. (MSC.248(83), Annex, para 1.1.1)

when.x: Each ship should submit a full report in accordance with paragraph 3.2.1 as soon as it crosses the boundary to enter the ship reporting system. (para 3.3.1; for ships that must report, should is to be read as shall)
Each ship should submit a report in accordance with paragraph 3.2.2 as soon as it crosses the boundary to leave the ship reporting system. (para 3.3.2)
Further reports should be made whenever there is a change in navigation status or circumstances, particularly in relation to item Q of the reporting format. (para 3.3.3)

how.n: Primary: send by Inmarsat-C (or ship's email) as a direct email; NOAA pays Inmarsat-C costs (50 CFR 404 Appendix E). Do not use batch message routing services. Address from 50 CFR 404.4(d), (e). MSC.279(85) prints it as "nwhi.notifications@noaa-gov", an obvious misprint; the US rule and the 2007 text use @noaa.gov.
In a developing emergency, to request response and assistance (MSC.248(83) para 5.2). Number as printed in 2007; not re-confirmed.
For US vessels under 300 GT without email (50 CFR 404.4(f)).
For US vessels under 300 GT without email (50 CFR 404.4(f)).

Vessel draft in meters: maximum present static draft in meters decimal centimeters // (e.g. O/11.50//)

Contact information of ship's agent or owner: name/address/and phone number //
Ship size (length overall and gross tonnage) and type: LOA in meters decimal centimeters/gross tons/type of ship // (e.g. U/294.14/54592/CONTAINER SHIP//)
Persons: total number of persons on board // (e.g. W/15//)

fn: Lines above are the ENTRY report (50 CFR 404 Appendix E, table E.1; the IMO list in MSC.248(83) para 3.2.1 is A, B, C or D, E or F, I, L, O, P, Q or R, T, U, W). The EXIT report is CORAL SHIPREP //, A, B (date, time and month of exit), C and R (Appendix E table E.3; IMO para 3.2.2 lists A, B, C or D). The automatic system rejects reports that do not follow the exact format: no extra text, extraneous characters or double spacing. Hazardous cargo details may be sent by non-verbal means before entering. Language English.

ver: Outer boundary points 1 to 19 and the arc centres 20 and 21 read from MSC.279(85) Annex para 2 (IMO PDF pages 2 and 3) by pdftotext and a regex, then re-read by eye against the page. Arc points (9a1 to 9a7, 19a1 to 19a7) were computed on a sphere at the printed radius; the printed end points lie 60.2 NM from their centres, which confirms the radius. Who must report from MSC.248(83) para 1; address, report syntax and exit report from 50 CFR 404.4 and Appendix E (eCFR, 2026-10-01).
nt: The reporting area is the band between the outer boundary and the Areas To Be Avoided (ATBA): you report when you cross the outer boundary inward and again when you cross it outward. The ATBA circles and connecting areas (listed in area_quote) are the inner limit and must be avoided anyway. Two parts of the outer boundary are arcs, not straight lines: points 9 to 10 (round Nihoa, east end) and 19 to 1 (round Kure, west end); the points named 9a1 to 9a7 and 19a1 to 19a7 are computed along those arcs only to draw them and are flagged inferred. Discrepancy: the US regulation 50 CFR 404 Appendix D still lists the original 2007 outer boundary of MSC.248(83) (100 points, slightly different, e.g. point 1 29 25.47N 178 16.97W), while IMO replaced it in MSC.279(85) (in force 1 June 2009). This record follows the IMO text; the difference is small (about 1 to 10 NM). The Monument was enlarged in 2016 and became a National Marine Sanctuary in 2025; those larger limits are NOT the reporting area. The IMO title calls it a ship reporting system; it is mandatory only for the ships in applies_to (via US port entry conditions) and recommended for others.

t: Right whale mandatory ship reporting system, north-eastern United States (WHALESNORTH)
au: United States Coast Guard (shore-based authority); system run with NOAA Fisheries
ap: Every self-propelled ship of 300 gross tons or more. Government ships exempt under SOLAS are encouraged to report.
apq: Each self-propelled ship of 300 gross tons or greater must participate in the reporting systems, except government ships exempted from reporting by regulation V/8-1(c) of SOLAS. However, exempt ships are encouraged to participate in the reporting systems. (33 CFR 169.125)

when.x: Participating ships must report to the shore-based authority upon entering the area covered by a reporting system. Additional reports are not necessary for movements made within a system or for ships exiting a system. (33 CFR 169.130) The mandatory ship reporting system in the northeastern United States operates year-round. (33 CFR 169.110)

ln.x: INMARSAT Number: vessel INMARSAT number.
Ship: the name, call sign or ship station identity, IMO number, and flag of the vessel.
Date and time of event: a 6-digit group giving day of month (first two digits), hours and minutes (last four digits).
True course: a 3-digit group indicating true course.
Speed in knots and tenths of knots: a 3-digit group.

Date, time and point of entry into system: entry time expressed as in (B) and entry position as a 4-digit latitude group with N or S and a 5-digit longitude group with E or W, or true bearing and distance in nautical miles from a clearly identified landmark.
Destination and expected time of arrival: name of port and date time group expressed as in (B).
Route information: intended track.

fn: Message starts with the system identifier line (WHALESNORTH//). Each line is the letter, a slash, the data and ends with //, as in the US Coast Pilot example (e.g. H/031410Z APR/4104N/06918W//, L/WP/4104N/06918W/15.5//; several L lines allowed). US Coast Pilot: extra greetings or comments in the message stop the automatic system from accepting it. nt: Report once, when entering the area. Not needed when leaving a port inside the area or when leaving the area. The boundary runs from point 1 through point 7 and then follows the Massachusetts shoreline back to point 1 (Cape Cod Bay and Massachusetts Bay). Coordinates are NAD 83 in the US rule (same values as the IMO text). The return message gives recent right whale sightings and precautions; if no return message comes, US Coast Pilot says to tell the local USCG Sector office. Separate US rules also apply here, not covered by this record: speed limits of 10 knots in Seasonal Management Areas (50 CFR 224.105), the 500 yard approach limit (50 CFR 224.103), the Boston TSS and the seasonal Great South Channel area to be avoided.

t: Right whale mandatory ship reporting system, south-eastern United States (WHALESSOUTH)
au: United States Coast Guard (shore-based authority); system run with NOAA Fisheries
ap: Every self-propelled ship of 300 gross tons or more, during the season 15 November to 15 April (US rule says to 16 April). Government ships exempt under SOLAS are encouraged to report.
apq: Each self-propelled ship of 300 gross tons or greater must participate in the reporting systems, except government ships exempted from reporting by regulation V/8-1(c) of SOLAS. However, exempt ships are encouraged to participate in the reporting systems. (33 CFR 169.125)

when.x: Participating ships must report to the shore-based authority upon entering the area covered by a reporting system. Additional reports are not necessary for movements made within a system or for ships exiting a system. (33 CFR 169.130) The mandatory ship reporting system in the southeastern United States operates during the period beginning on November 15 each year through April 16 of the following year. (33 CFR 169.120)

ln.x: INMARSAT Number: vessel INMARSAT number.
Ship: the name, call sign or ship station identity, IMO number, and flag of the vessel.
Date and time of event: a 6-digit group giving day of month (first two digits), hours and minutes (last four digits).
True course: a 3-digit group indicating true course.
Speed in knots and tenths of knots: a 3-digit group.

aq: Southeastern United States. Geographical boundaries of the proposed southeast area include coastal waters within about 25 nautical miles along a 90 nautical miles stretch of the Atlantic seaboard in Florida and Georgia (Appendix 2). The area extends from the shoreline east to longitude 80°51'.60 W with the southern and northern boundary at latitudes 30°00'.00 N and 31°27'.00 N, respectively. NOAA Chart No.11009. (MSC.85(70), Annex 1, para 2.2)

nt: The IMO text gives only three limits: latitude 31 27.00N (north), latitude 30 00.00N (south) and longitude 080 51.60W (east); the coast closes the area on the west. The two corner points on 080 51.60W are the exact meeting points of those printed limits but are not printed as points, so they are flagged inferred. The two coast points are only approximate positions where the latitude limits meet the Georgia and Florida coast; they are there to draw the map and are NOT official. Season: the US regulation (33 CFR 169.120) says 15 November through 16 April; the IMO resolution and US Coast Pilot 1 say 15 November through 15 April. Report if in doubt. Report once on entering; no report when leaving a port inside the area or leaving the area. Separate US rules (Seasonal Management Area speed limit of 10 knots, 500 yard approach limit, recommended routes into Brunswick, Fernandina and Jacksonville) are not covered by this record.

t: Great Barrier Reef and Torres Strait ship reporting system (REEFREP), reported to Reef VTS
au: Reef VTS (Great Barrier Reef and Torres Strait Vessel Traffic Service), operated by Maritime Safety Queensland from Townsville and Gladstone VTS centres, authorised by AMSA (Marine Orders 63 and 64)
res: MSC.52(66), amended by MSC.161(78) and MSC.315(88)
ap: Ships of 50 m or more overall; all oil tankers, liquefied gas carriers, chemical tankers and ships under the INF Code whatever their length; ships towing or pushing, or being towed or pushed, or where the tow is 150 m or more.
apq: The following categories of ships must report to Reef VTS: All ships with an overall length of 50 metres or more; All oil tankers, liquefied gas carriers, chemical tankers or ships coming within the Irradiated Nuclear Fuel Code, including those with an overall length of less than 50 metres; and Ships which are towing or pushing, or being towed or pushed, or where the overall length of the tow is 150 meters or more (the overall length of the tow is measured from the stern of the towing vessel to the after end of the tow). (Reef VTS User Guide 2025, section 5.1.1)

when.x: Reef VTS must receive an ER at least one (1) hour before a ship: Enters the REEFREP area; or Departs from a port within the REEFREP area. (User Guide 2025, section 8)
The following information must be provided to Reef VTS immediately on exiting the Reef VTS area or arriving at a port in the Reef VTS area. (section 8.2.2)

If the ship needs to deviate from the Route Plan which was given to Reef VTS on entry to the Reef VTS area, this should be reported to Reef VTS before the deviation is made. In situations where a deviation is made without much warning, a DR report should be sent to Reef VTS within 15 minutes after the deviation made. (section 8.2.3)

Where Reef VTS advises that the ship's position is being tracked by sensors then an IP is not required. If the ship's position is not being tracked by sensors, then a brief position report must be provided to Reef VTS. (section 8.2.4)

Defect Report (IR): immediately if a ship suffers damage, failure or breakdown which affects the ship's safety, or, immediately if there is pollution or cargo lost overboard, or, special reports as defined by the IMO for incidents involving dangerous goods, harmful substances or marine pollutants. (section 8.2.5)

Date and time (UTC) (e.g. B/010200UTC)

Next Port of Call and ETA UTC (e.g. I/Gladstone/050500UTC NOV 16)
Pilot Company Details: give the pilot company name (e.g. J/Torres Pilots or J/Auriga)
Date, time (UTC) and point of exit from area (e.g. K/042100UTC/SANDY CAPE or K/042100UTC/2420S 15110E)
Route information: recommended standard route plans, taking into account vessel draught (e.g. L/INNER ROUTE DEEP DRAUGHT or L/ALPHA NORTH VIA VARZIN PASSAGE/HANNIBAL)
Communication methods: Inmarsat C details, IMN, manufacturer, model, and ship's satellite phone number (e.g. M1/423456789/JRC/JUE- 85C or M2/870773123456)
Draught: fore and aft and deepest draught, in meters and decimeters (e.g. O/Fore 11.6/Aft 11.8/Deepest 11.8)
Cargo on-board: normal name of cargo and whether it is classified as hazardous (yes or no) (e.g. P/BULK CHEMICALS/ DG YES). May be given by non-voice means before the first Reef VTS report.
Defects, damage, deficiencies, or other limitations (e.g. Q/Include details as required)
Ship type, length (meters) and gross tonnage (e.g. U/TANKER/180/28000)
Remarks: any additional information which would help the navigational safety of shipping in the Reef VTS area (e.g. abnormal weather, faulty navigational aid, DG, HS or MP incident reports)

fn: Lines above are the Entry Report (ER, Table 3 of the 2025 guide; * = required). Note that the ER has no E line. Final Report FR: A and K. Route Deviation DR: A, B, K, L, O required, I optional. Intermediate Position IP: A, C, F required, B optional. Defect Report IR: A, C, F, Q. The first line gives the message type (ID/ER, ID/FR, ...). Language English, IMO SMCP. Outer ports (Port Alma, Mackay, Whitsundays, Abbot Point, Lucinda, Mourilyan, Cape Flattery) also need ER and FR to Reef VTS and a call to the local VTS on arrival and departure (Table 8). Passenger ships have extra rules (section 8.3).

pts.nm: end of the outer edge of the Great Barrier Reef section

aq: 2.1 The reporting system will cover the general area, as shown in the chartlet at appendix 1. The area encompasses the Torres Strait between longitudes 141º 45′ E and 144º 00′ E, including the Endeavour Strait, and the waters of the Great Barrier Reef (GBR) between the Australian coast and the outer edge of the GBR, from the latitude of Cape York (10º 40′ S) south-eastwards to 21° 00′ S 152° 55′ E. From this position, the REEFREP boundary extends as follows: (a) to position 23° 42′ S 153° 45′ E, (b) thence to position 24° 30′ S 153° 35′ E, (c) thence westward on latitude 24° 30′ S to its intersection with the Queensland coastline at the low water mark, and (d) thence generally north-westerly along the coastline to the latitude of Cape York (10º 40′ S). 2.2 The REEFREP area is shown on charts AUS 4620 (1996) and AUS 4635 (2010). (MSC.315(88), Annex para 1)

nt: Area: only the southern closing line is given by coordinates (points 1 to 3, then west along 24 30S to the coast). The rest of the boundary is described in words: the Torres Strait between longitudes 141 45E and 144 00E (including the Endeavour Strait), and the waters between the coast and the outer edge of the Great Barrier Reef from 10 40S to 21 00S 152 55E. The outer reef edge is not given as coordinates in the IMO text; use the chartlet or charts AUS 4620 and AUS 4635. Point 4 is only an approximate coast position. Reef VTS is split into North and South at latitude 18 00S (separate emails and Inmarsat SACs). Rules changed: the 1996 system used VHF channels 5, 18 and 19 and a centre at Hay Point; the 2004 amendment asked for the entry report 2 hours before entry; the current Reef VTS guide (2025) asks for at least 1 hour and uses VHF CH 11 and 14. Masters must keep a listening watch on the Reef VTS working channels and keep Inmarsat-C logged into POR. Coastal pilotage, under keel clearance and designated shipping area rules also apply but are not covered here. Penalties under Navigation Act 2012 s215 and s216.

t: Straits of Malacca and Singapore mandatory ship reporting system (STRAITREP)
cty: Malaysia and Singapore (with Indonesia as a littoral State)
au: Klang VTS (sectors 1 to 5) and Johor VTS (sector 6), Marine Department Malaysia; Singapore VTS (sectors 7 to 9), Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore
ap: Ships of 300 GT and above; ships of 50 m or more; tows or pushed units of 300 GT or 50 m combined; ships of any size carrying hazardous cargo; all passenger ships fitted with VHF; smaller ships with VHF that use the traffic lane or separation zone in an emergency.
apq: Ships of the following categories are required to participate in the ship reporting system: .1 vessels of 300 GT and above; .2 vessels of 50 metres or more in length; .3 vessels engaged in towing or pushing with a combined GT of 300 and above, or with a combined length of 50 metres or more; .4 vessels of any tonnage carrying hazardous cargo, as defined in paragraph 1.4 of resolution MSC.43(64); .5 all passenger vessels that are fitted with VHF, regardless of length or GT; and .6 any category of vessels less than 50 metres in length or less than 300 GT which are fitted with VHF and in an emergency, uses the appropriate traffic lane or separation zone, in order to avoid immediate danger. (MSC.73(69), Annex 1, para 1.1)

when.x: Ships entering the operational area shall report when crossing the limits mentioned in paragraph 3 or when crossing a line joining Tg. Piai (01°15'.50N 103°30'.75E) and Pulau Karimun Kecil (01°09'.20N 103°24'.35E) or when leaving port or anchorages in the area or before joining the traffic lane of the TSS. (para 3.3.1)

Ships entering the operational area shall also report when approaching from the south via Selat Riau, abeam of Karang Galang Lt. (01°09'.58N 104°11'.47E) or via Selat Durian, report when Pulau Jangkat Beacon (00°57'.89N 103°42'72E) is abeam and when approaching from the East Johor Strait, abeam of Eastern Buoy (01°17'.87N, 104°05'.99E). (para 3.3.2)

A ship approaching from any direction other than those specified above shall on reaching sector 7, sector 8 or sector 9 as appropriate report by giving the vessel's position in term of bearing and distance from one of the following reference points: Pu Iyu Kechil Lt (01°11'.48N 103°21'.23E), Sultan Shoal Lt (01°14'.38N 103°38'.98E), Raffles Lt (01°09'.60N 103°44'.55E), Sakijang Lt Bn (01°13'.30N 103°51'.37E), Bedok Lt (01°18'.54N 103°56'.06E), Tg. Stapa Lt (01°20'.57N 104°08'.24E), Horsburgh Lt (01°19'.81N 104°24'.44E). As an alternative the position can also be given in latitude and longitude. (para 3.3.3)

ln.x: Ship: name of ship, call sign, IMO identification number (if available).
Position: a 4-digit group giving latitude in degrees and minutes suffixed with N or S and a 5-digit group giving longitude in degrees and minutes suffixed with E or W (C or D).
Position: true bearing (first 3 digits) and distance in nautical miles from a clearly identifiable point (state landmark), instead of C.

Speed in knots and tenths of knots: a 3-digit group. When requested by VTS authority.
Hazardous cargo on board: indicate Yes or No to whether vessel is carrying hazardous cargo. If Yes the class if applicable.

Description of pollution or dangerous goods lost overboard: brief detail of type of pollution (oil, chemicals, etc.) or dangerous goods lost overboard; position expressed as in (C) or (D).

aq: The operational area of STRAITREP covers the Straits of Malacca and Singapore between longitudes 100°40'E and 104°23'E as shown in the chartlets attached as appendix 1 and appendix 2. The area includes the routeing system in the Straits of Malacca and Singapore. The area is divided into nine sectors, each has an assigned VHF channel as shown in appendix 3. The reference charts which include the operational area of STRAITREP are the Malaysian Chart Series MAL 515, 521 and 523 of the Hydrographer, Royal Malaysian Navy or the equivalent charts published by the competent hydrographic authority. (MSC.73(69), Annex 1, paras 2.1 and 2.2)

nt: The IMO text gives the area only as the strait between longitudes 100 40E and 104 23E; the limits between the nine sectors are shown only on the chartlets (images), so this record has no sector boundaries. The four points are flagged inferred: they only draw the two limiting meridians across the strait. Report on entering at the western or eastern limit, at the Tg Piai to Pulau Karimun Kecil line, on leaving a port or anchorage in the area, before joining a TSS lane, or at the southern approach points (Selat Riau, Selat Durian, East Johor Strait). Channel 88 is used in sectors 2, 5 and 6: check the sector before calling. The Pulau Jangkat Beacon longitude is printed '103°42'72E' (the decimal point is missing in the source; most likely 103°42'.72E). Rules for vessels navigating through the Straits of Malacca and Singapore and the TSS also apply. Singapore port arrivals have separate port reporting rules (not covered).
